page: Amazon Web Services r7a.large is an entry-level memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and fourth-generation AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs running at a base clock speed of 3.7 GHz with single-thread-per-core allocation. The CPU features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 8 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AVX512_BF16, and hardware cryptography instructions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Memory capacity is configured with 16.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory clocked at 5 GHz, delivering an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio typical of memory-optimized profiles. The server features no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage via Amazon EBS, and operates with a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. No dedicated hardware GPUs are attached to this instance profile.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core compute performance, with stress-ng single-core registering 3076.88 and Geekbench single-core scoring 1980.0, both placing in the top 25 percent. Conversely, aggregate multi-core throughput remains constrained by the 2-vCPU core count, reflected in a Geekbench multi-core score of 3572.0 and PassMark database score of 1801.74. Memory bandwidth reaches 36.7 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 27.09 GB/sec for writes. In application benchmarks, Redis throughput reaches 5.29 million SET operations per second, while LLM inference achieves 160.95 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model, falling to 7.38 tokens per second on a 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, r7a.large offers an accessible entry point to modern DDR5 memory and high single-threaded performance without the commitment of larger multithreaded systems. The lack of bundled local NVMe storage and modest 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth represent key architectural tradeoffs. The instance is suited for small-scale in-memory caches, lightweight relational databases, microservices requiring high RAM per core, and background worker jobs that benefit from strong single-core CPU frequency.
description: Amazon Web Services r7a.large is a memory-optimized instance engineered for workloads demanding an elevated memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside modern compute capabilities. Powered by the Nitro hypervisor and AMD EPYC 9R14 x86_64 processors clocked at 3.7 GHz, it features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs supported by 16.0 GB of 5 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding 8.0 GB per core. It includes no bundled local storage, relies on external EBS volumes, provides a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps, and contains no hardware accelerators. Benchmark testing shows strong single-core execution with high stress-ng and Geekbench single-core figures, while overall throughput is bounded by the low core count. The server offers a cost-effective allocation of high-speed DDR5 capacity for single-node caching systems, development databases, and memory-intensive microservices.
